narrative.overview: A chambers library after hours. Deep green walls, brass and oxblood, one reading lamp, and the advocate's documents standing on a shelf as books. Drafting happens on a lit folio: the description is typed, ink drains from the well while Lawie works, the draft is written in, and a brass seal lands when the advocate finalises. Daylight is the same room with the curtains open, not an inverted palette. The system is paper-and-ink, not glass-and-gradient: flat, square-cornered, hairline-bordered surfaces; depth from one card shadow and the lamp pool; motion that is literal and rare.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (brass) for action, used sparingly; oxblood only for books and destructive confirms.
Square corners (0 to 4px); pills only for chips.
Serif display (Tiro Devanagari Hindi) above 20px, humanist sans (Mukta) below, both carrying Devanagari natively.
Four signature objects: the folio, the inkwell, the seal, the shelf of spines.
Mobile first at 360px; every effect degrades to a still image on phones, under reduced motion, and when the tab is hidden.

rules.name: The Brass Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: Brass fill is never used for text under 20px. Brass Text is the text form; the two are different tokens on purpose.

rules.name: The One Primary Rule
rules.body: One brass-filled button per screen. Everything else is ghost or a link.

rules.name: The Status Pair Rule
rules.body: A status colour is always used as its text token on its soft token, or as its text token on Card. Never as a fill behind white text.

rules.name: The Twenty Pixel Rule
rules.body: Headings at 20px and above are Tiro; below 20px they are Mukta 500. There is no third face and no third weight.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can sit in a column is set with tabular numerals.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is one card shadow and it belongs to the object the advocate is working on. Two shadowed things on one screen is one too many.

rules.name: The No Nested Card Rule
rules.body: Cards do not sit inside cards. Inside the folio, structure is spacing and hairlines.

dos: Do set every number with tabular numerals and keep Ink as a number plus the word Ink (never a draft count).
Do build both themes from the same token names; a component that reads one literal colour is a bug.
Do keep the lamp follow and the dust motes behind (pointer: fine) and (min-width: 900px), and pause every loop on visibilitychange.
Do give every screen its loading, empty and error state before it ships, with Retry on every error.
Do keep running text at or under 65 characters a line and Muted text at 12px or larger.
Do show a status in text as well as colour (the spine's label, the chip's words).
donts: Don't use brass fill as text, or any colour but Brass Text for links.
Don't put two brass-filled buttons on one screen.
Don't round a card, the folio, an input or a dialog beyond 4px; pills are for chips and the seal.
Don't add a shadow, a gradient or a glass effect anywhere the system does not name one.
Don't nest a card in a card, or a border inside a border.
Don't add a third typeface, a third Mukta weight, or an icon font; icons are inline SVG at 16 to 24px.
Don't let an effect be the only cue: hover, the lamp and the pen are decoration, never information.
Don't write copy into a component; signed copy comes in as props from the Ajay-signed copy files.
